title: Natural affine model presentation over the original local ring
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $x\in Y$, and $U\subseteq Y$ an affine open containing $x$. Put $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $S=\mathcal O_{Y,x}$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor], with $A\to S$ the germ map. Let $T$ be the associated-module functor [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] followed by restriction along $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$. There is a family of $S$-linear equivalences $\delta_{F,M,e}:S\otimes_A M\xrightarrow{\sim}F_x$ for every sheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], every $A$-module $M$, and every model isomorphism $e:F|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}T(M)$. For morphisms $c:F\to G$ and $d:M\to N$ and model isomorphisms $e_F,e_G$ satisfying $e_G\circ(c|_U)=T(d)\circ e_F$, the identity $c_x(\delta_{F,M,e_F}(t))=\delta_{G,N,e_G}((S\otimes_A d)(t))$ holds for every $t\in S\otimes_A M$.

source.place: Lemma 17.10.5 (3); Tag 01HV, Lemma 26.5.4 (6)-(7) and functoriality; local-ring presentation part of new-e1-affine-model-stalk-tensor-transport

proof.text: Put xU=(x,hx) in U and q=isoSpec(xU). Mathlib Scheme.Modules.restrictStalkNatIso, first for U.ι and then for U.2.isoSpec.hom, and the stalk of e identify F_x with (tilde M)_q. These additive maps are semilinear over the corresponding invertible stalk-ring maps: on germs on a common neighborhood the formula is epsilon(r smul m)=alpha inverse(r) smul epsilon(m), by germ_restrictStalkNatIso_hom_app, the inverse ring germ formula, and germ_smul. Germ representatives reduce all scalars and elements to this calculation. The chart ring map transports the germ A->S to the canonical map A->O_SpecA,q (isoSpec_hom_appTop and germ_stalkMap_apply). Thus the composite identification is linear over the identified stalk rings. The maps are fixed functorially before any module is chosen.

The statement [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] gives both the ring localization O_SpecA,q=A_q and the module localization tilde.toStalk M q at the complement of q. Transfer the ring localization along the preceding stalk-ring isomorphism (also Mathlib IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_stalk) and the module localization along the preceding semilinear module isomorphism. This gives a localization map M->F_x compatible with the germ A->S. IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange and its equiv give the S-linear equivalence delta:S tensor_A M->F_x, sending s tensor m to s times the transported tilde germ of m.

Take stalks of the supplied commuting square and use naturality of the restriction-stalk isomorphisms and the tilde germ maps. This gives the naturality equality on 1 tensor m. Both sides are S-linear, so it holds on s tensor m, and tensor induction extends it to all t. All constructions also work for the zero module; an empty open admits no point satisfying hx. No global quasi-coherence of F is required.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_affine_model_stalk_presentation
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (x : Y) (U : Y.affineOpens) (hx : x ∈ U.1) :
    let A := (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u)
    let S := (Y.presheaf.stalk x : Type u)
    letI : Algebra A S := (Y.presheaf.germ U.1 x hx).hom.toAlgebra
    let T := tilde.functor Γ(Y, U.1) ⋙ Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.2.isoSpec.hom
    ∃ δ : ∀ (F : Y.Modules) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A),
      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.1.ι).obj F ≅ T.obj M) →
        (S ⊗[A] M) ≃ₗ[S] F.presheaf.stalk x,
      ∀ (F G : Y.Modules) (M N : ModuleCat.{u} A) (c : F ⟶ G) (d : M ⟶ N)
        (eF : (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.1.ι).obj F ≅ T.obj M)
        (eG : (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.1.ι).obj G ≅ T.obj N),
        (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.1.ι).map c ≫ eG.hom = eF.hom ≫ T.map d →
        ∀ t, c.stalkLinearMap x (δ F M eF t) =
          δ G N eG (d.hom.baseChange S t)
